concepts.label: evpn-instance
concepts.gloss: An evpn-instance (EVI / MAC-VRF) is the EVPN-layer L2 forwarding/tenant instance that represents a tenant's MAC-VRF and is realized on one or more attachment-circuits (ACs) to provide that tenant's Ethernet service.
concepts.example: EVI-5000 (MAC-VRF ACME) is the EVPN instance for the ACME tenant and is realized on attachment-circuits such as AC-PE1 and AC-PE2 to carry the tenant's MAC learning and forwarding.

concepts.label: attachment-circuit
concepts.gloss: An attachment-circuit (AC / access-interface) is the physical or logical customer-facing interface on a PE that carries a customer's traffic and is placed into (mapped into) a specific evpn-instance (EVI).
concepts.example: AC-PE1 is an attachment circuit on PE1 that is configured into EVI-5000 to carry the ACME tenant's Ethernet traffic.

concepts.label: vpn-network-access
concepts.gloss: A vpn-network-access endpoint is the customer-facing endpoint identifier (for example a subinterface, S-VLAN or CE-facing port) that is located at a particular attachment-circuit and represents the CE's attachment into the EVPN service.
concepts.example: ep-PE1 is a VPN network access endpoint located at AC-PE1 and represents the CE attachment point for the ACME tenant within EVI-5000.

concepts.label: bridge-domain
concepts.gloss: A bridge-domain (bridge-vlan / VLAN) is the L2 broadcast/forwarding domain inside an evpn-instance that groups customer MACs (often corresponding to a VLAN ID) for switching within that EVI.
concepts.example: bd-vlan-200 is the bridge-domain for VLAN 200 within EVI-5000, carrying all customer frames associated with that L2 domain.

concepts.label: ingress-policer
concepts.gloss: An ingress-policer (rate-limiter) is a rate-control object applied on an attachment-circuit to limit or police incoming traffic toward the EVPN instance on that AC.
concepts.example: policer-200/50 is configured on AC-PE1 to police ingress traffic into EVI-5000 (for example limiting the entered traffic rate according to the policer profile).

concepts.label: traffic-class
concepts.gloss: A traffic-class (forwarding-class / class) is a CoS/forwarding classification defined inside an evpn-instance used to map and treat traffic (e.g., EF, BE) for queuing and forwarding decisions within that MAC-VRF.
concepts.example: EF-class is a traffic-class defined in EVI-5000 to identify and forward low-latency traffic with expedited forwarding treatment.

concepts.label: mac-vrf-learning
concepts.gloss: mac-vrf-learning (local MAC learning) is the per-attachment-circuit configuration that enables the PE to perform local MAC address learning on that AC (as opposed to relying solely on control-plane EVPN advertisements).
concepts.example: local learning @AC-PE1 enables the PE at AC-PE1 to learn and populate local MAC entries for EVI-5000 from observed frames on that attachment-circuit.

concepts.label: interface-mtu
concepts.gloss: An interface-mtu (MTU) is the framing-size configuration applied on an attachment-circuit that sets the maximum transmit/receive frame size allowed on that access interface feeding the EVPN service.
concepts.example: MTU 9100 is set on AC-PE2 to allow jumbo frames on the attachment-circuit that feeds EVI-5000.

concepts.label: ethernet-segment
concepts.gloss: An ethernet-segment (ESI / segment) is the multihoming identifier representing a single customer Ethernet attachment that spans multiple attachment-circuits (and typically multiple PEs) to enable EVPN multihoming behavior for the associated EVI.
concepts.example: ESI-0011 (dual-homed) identifies the customer Ethernet segment that spans AC-PE1 and AC-PE2, enabling the CE to be multihomed into EVI-5000 across both attachment-circuits.

concepts.label: MAC-mobility
concepts.gloss: MAC-mobility (MAC-move) is the EVPN L2-control mechanism inside an evpn-instance that records and propagates that a particular MAC has moved between attachment-circuits so remote PEs can update forwarding (often using mobility sequence information).
concepts.example: mobility seq=3 for a moved MAC indicates that within EVI-5000 a given MAC address has been seen to move and the mobility sequence number 3 is used in EVPN advertisements to update remote forwarding tables.
instances: mobility seq=3 for a moved MAC

concepts.label: vendor-evi-tag
concepts.gloss: A vendor-evi-tag (proprietary evi tag) is an opaque, vendor-specific identifier or tag attached to an evpn-instance used for proprietary segmentation or metadata that is not part of the standard EVPN model.
concepts.example: vendor-evi-tag on EVI-5000 is a vendor-proprietary tag applied to the ACME tenant's EVI to convey device-specific metadata or mapping that other vendors may not interpret.
